title: Constrained Optimization to Train Neural Networks on Critical and Under-Represented Classes
authors: Sara Sangalli, Ertunc Erdil, Andreas Hoetker, Olivio Donati, Ender Konukoglu
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021), vol. 34
conclusions: Poses training a binary-classification DNN under class imbalance as a constrained optimization problem, with a novel constraint (built on Mann-Whitney/AUC statistics) that favors reducing FPR at high TPR for the minority/critical class.

Solves the constrained problem via an Augmented Lagrangian Method (ALM): per-critical-sample Lagrange multipliers plus a quadratic penalty, with the penalty coefficient mu increased on a schedule when a validation metric fails to improve.
Extends the binary constraint to multi-class classification with two variants (ALM_m,1 and ALM_m,2), the second also pushing down non-critical-class probability on critical samples.
Evaluated on an in-house prostate MRI dataset, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 (binary and long-tailed multi-class variants), combined with 9 existing imbalance-handling losses as the base loss F(theta).

Shows the ALM constraint improves FPR-at-high-TPR and AUC over the un-constrained baselines in the majority of loss/imbalance-ratio combinations, and outperforms directly optimizing AUC via mini-batch AUC (MBAUC).

The constraint operates purely on a per-sample/pairwise margin (AUC-style ranking), not on any test-set / transductive prediction-COUNT constraint; there is no notion of a hard cap on how many items may receive a given label.
